Carmen (Finance): Heads-up: morning billing run created two PDFs for customer Lumenix. One PDF total = $7,920, other = $5,220. Missing discount line for reserved GPUs of -$2,700.
Marco (Billing): Yep I see invoice ids 2026-04-LX-0153 and 2026-04-LX-0153-copy. Ledger shows same invoice_id on both.
Iris (Billing-ops): DevBot flagged rendering warning: pdf_render: duplicate_invoice_id detected for run 1795005600.
DevBot: job=billing.batch run=1795005600 status=partial_fail duplicates=1 missing_lines=1 artifact=/tmp/lumenix_diff_1795.csv
Noah (Engineering): looks like a compose race: two workers attempted to emit the same invoice_id after we split large accounts across shards. One worker dropped the reserved_capacity line because of a streaming flush error.
Iris (Billing-ops): Can we recompose only Lumenix? Want to avoid full batch rerun. Also need to void the bad PDF before customer sees it.
Noah (Engineering): We have a targeted compose endpoint. I'll POST recompose for account=lumenix. Also adding guard to ensure invoice_id uniqueness before pdf publish.
Marco (Billing): Void step done: marked 2026-04-LX-0153-copy as void, note=PDF duplicated due to compose race. Preparing corrected invoice 2026-04-LX-0153-R1.
Zoey (Acct Exec): Please include an apology blurb and the credit memo. I'll sign off.
Carmen (Finance): Credit memo for $2,700 approved. Marco, attach subscription ids and reconciliation CSV to the message.
Iris (Billing-ops): Recompose successful, reserved_capacity row present in R1. Uploaded sanitized csv to artifacts.
DevBot: artifact=/artifacts/BLG-5903/lumenix_recompose_1795009000.csv status=uploaded
Marco (Billing): Sent corrected invoice + credit memo to customer and CC'd Zoey. Voided duplicate noted in ledger entry LN-7452.
Noah (Engineering): Patch merged to prevent double-emit; added alert for duplicate_invoice_id > 0.
Carmen (Finance): Closing loop 14; corrected invoice issued, credit memo sent, fix merged. Reopen if anything else crops up.
_meta: generated_for_dataset: finance invoice generation failures; style: concise Slack thread with bot lines and actions
